companies.name: Estée Lauder Companies
companies.business_model: Prestige multi-brand beauty conglomerate. Manufactures, markets, and sells skincare, makeup, fragrance, and haircare products through department stores, specialty retailers, e-commerce, and company-owned stores globally. Revenue is split across product categories and geographies, with heavy reliance on travel retail and Asia-Pacific markets.
companies.target_audience: Women aged 25–65. Prestige and luxury beauty channels globally.
companies.notes: One of the largest prestige beauty groups globally. Has faced significant headwinds from Asia-Pacific slowdown and travel retail decline post-2022.

companies.name: Ulta Beauty
companies.business_model: Specialty beauty retailer operating over 1,400 physical stores across the U.S., complemented by a growing e-commerce platform. Unique positioning as an all-price-point retailer offering both prestige and mass-market beauty brands under one roof, alongside in-store salon services. Revenue primarily from product sales; loyalty program (Ultamate Rewards) is central to retention strategy.
companies.target_audience: Women aged 18–45. ~44 million Ultamate Rewards active members (FY2024).
companies.notes: Largest specialty beauty retailer in the U.S. Known for combining prestige and mass beauty in one retail format. Partnership with Target expands reach significantly.

companies.name: e.l.f. Beauty
companies.business_model: Value-oriented beauty brand selling affordable cosmetics, skincare, and body care primarily through mass retail channels (Walmart, Target, CVS, Walgreens) and direct-to-consumer online. Known for rapid product development cycles, strong digital marketing, and manufacturing primarily in China at low cost. Operates lean and reinvests heavily in marketing.
companies.target_audience: Gen Z and Millennials aged 16–30. #1 mass cosmetics brand among teens (Piper Sandler, 2024).
companies.notes: One of the fastest-growing beauty companies in the U.S. in recent years. Exceptionally strong TikTok and social media presence. Acquisitive growth strategy via brands like Naturium.

companies.name: Coty Inc.
companies.headquarters: Amsterdam, Netherlands (operational HQ in New York, USA)
companies.business_model: Global beauty company operating across two divisions: Prestige (fragrances, skincare under licensed luxury brands) and Consumer Beauty (mass-market cosmetics, haircare, body care). Licenses brand names from luxury fashion houses for fragrance lines. Revenue is global with strong European and Americas presence.
companies.target_audience: Mass beauty consumers (Consumer division); fragrance buyers aged 25–55 (Prestige division).
companies.notes: Historically complex business with significant debt. Has been restructuring and divesting non-core assets. Kylie Jenner and Kim Kardashian brand stakes are held through Coty.

companies.name: Olaplex Holdings
companies.business_model: Single-brand, patent-protected professional haircare company. Products are built around a proprietary bond-building technology (Bis-Aminopropyl Diglycol Dimaleate). Sells through three channels: professional (salons), specialty retail (Sephora, Ulta), and direct-to-consumer. Asset-light model with third-party manufacturing.
companies.target_audience: Women aged 20–45 who colour or chemically treat hair. Sold in 100+ countries.
companies.notes: Experienced rapid growth post-IPO then significant decline due to consumer perception issues around product efficacy and market saturation. One of the most behaviourally interesting cases in this project.

companies.name: Sally Beauty Holdings
companies.business_model: Specialty beauty retailer and distributor operating through two segments: Sally Beauty Supply (retail stores open to public and licensed professionals) and Beauty Systems Group (professional-only distribution, including Armstrong McDowell stores). Sells professional-grade hair colour, haircare, nail, and skincare products at accessible prices.
companies.target_audience: DIY beauty consumers and licensed professionals aged 25–55. 4,800+ stores across 12 countries.
companies.notes: Brick-and-mortar heavy with over 4,800 stores globally. Has been working on digital transformation. Unique dual B2C and B2B model within beauty retail.

companies.name: Oddity Tech
companies.headquarters: New York City, NY, USA (with R&D in Tel Aviv)
companies.business_model: Digital-first, data-driven beauty and wellness company. Operates two direct-to-consumer brands online only, with no physical retail presence. Uses proprietary tech and data infrastructure to drive product development and personalisation. High gross margins due to DTC model. Invested heavily in AI-driven consumer matching and formulation.
companies.target_audience: Digitally native beauty consumers aged 20–40. 100% DTC, no physical retail.
companies.notes: Unique as a tech-forward beauty operator. Strong unit economics and DTC model. Relatively recent IPO (2023). AI-powered shade matching quiz is a core acquisition tool.

companies.name: L'Oréal
companies.business_model: Largest beauty company in the world by revenue. Operates across four divisions: Consumer Products (mass market), L'Oréal Luxe (prestige), Professional Products (salon), and Dermatological Beauty (pharmacy). Sells in 150+ countries. Business model is built on R&D investment, brand portfolio depth, and global distribution reach.
companies.target_audience: Global consumers across all demographics. Present in 150+ countries across four divisions.
companies.notes: Included as a global benchmark. Most challenging to analyse at company level for behavioural signals due to multi-brand structure. CeraVe and La Roche-Posay have been standout performers.

companies.name: Abercrombie & Fitch Co.
companies.founded_location: New York City, New York, USA
companies.business_model: Global omnichannel specialty apparel retailer operating through two brand segments: Abercrombie (adult) and Hollister (teen). Sells through company-owned stores and e-commerce globally. Known for a significant brand turnaround in the 2020s, shifting from exclusionary positioning to inclusive lifestyle brand.
companies.target_audience: Abercrombie: adults aged 20–35. Hollister: teens aged 15–22. 750+ stores globally.
companies.notes: One of the most compelling brand turnaround stories in retail. Strong financial recovery post-2022. CEO Fran Horowitz led significant repositioning. Good case for financial vs behavioural divergence.

companies.name: American Eagle Outfitters
companies.business_model: Specialty apparel retailer operating American Eagle (casual denim and apparel) and Aerie (intimates, activewear, swimwear) brands through stores and e-commerce. Aerie has been a key growth driver, known for its body-positive marketing. Also operates Quiet Platforms, a supply chain and logistics business.
companies.target_audience: Gen Z and Millennials aged 15–28. Aerie is one of the fastest-growing intimates brands in the US.
companies.notes: Aerie's body-positive brand identity has been a strong differentiator. Jeans are a core product category. Has faced margin pressure and supply chain challenges.

companies.name: Urban Outfitters Inc.
companies.business_model: Multi-brand lifestyle retail company operating through retail segment (Urban Outfitters, Free People, Anthropologie, Nuuly, Menus & Venues) and subscription/rental (Nuuly). Strong omnichannel presence. Each brand targets a distinct lifestyle consumer segment. Free People wholesale is a significant revenue contributor.
companies.target_audience: Urban Outfitters: 18–28. Free People: 25–35. Anthropologie: 30–50. All women-skewed.
companies.notes: Nuuly rental subscription is a differentiated and growing business unit. Strong brand portfolio with distinct identities. Free People wholesale adds B2B revenue.

companies.name: Gap Inc.
companies.business_model: Global apparel retail company operating four distinct brands across different consumer segments. Revenue from company-owned stores, e-commerce, franchise partnerships, and licensing. Has divested international operations in some regions and closed underperforming stores. Now focused on brand stabilisation and margin recovery.
companies.target_audience: Old Navy: families. Gap: 25–45. Banana Republic: professionals. Athleta: active women 30–50.
companies.notes: Old Navy is the largest revenue contributor. Company has struggled with brand coherence and has undergone significant restructuring. Athleta competes directly with Lululemon in the activewear space.

companies.name: Levi Strauss & Co.
companies.business_model: Global branded apparel company most closely associated with denim. Sells through wholesale (department stores, specialty retailers), company-owned stores, and growing DTC e-commerce. Three brands under portfolio. Iconic global brand with strong recognition across demographics. Revenue is globally distributed.
companies.target_audience: Broad demographic aged 18–45. Levi's sold in 110+ countries.
companies.notes: One of the world's oldest and most recognisable apparel brands. Has been actively growing DTC channel and reducing wholesale dependence. Dockers has been an underperformer.

companies.name: Revolve Group
companies.business_model: Digital-first fashion retailer with no physical stores. Uses a data-driven, influencer-led marketing model to curate and sell apparel, footwear, beauty, and lifestyle products from hundreds of brands, alongside its own private labels. Revenue is almost entirely e-commerce. FORWARD is its higher-end luxury companion platform.
companies.target_audience: Millennial and Gen Z women aged 18–35. ~2 million active customers (FY2024).
companies.notes: Pioneered influencer-driven e-commerce. REVOLVE Festival at Coachella is a signature brand moment. Has faced margin pressure and return rate challenges. Excellent behavioural signal candidate.

companies.name: Lululemon Athletica
companies.business_model: Premium activewear and lifestyle apparel brand selling through company-owned stores and e-commerce globally. Known for community-based marketing, ambassador programmes, and in-store yoga/fitness events. DTC-heavy revenue model with very high brand loyalty and repeat purchase rates. Entered footwear and self-care categories.
companies.target_audience: Active consumers aged 20–45. ~20 million loyalty members globally. Growing menswear segment.
companies.notes: One of the strongest brand loyalty cases in retail. Community flywheel and ambassador model are distinctive. MIRROR acquisition was unsuccessful and divested. International expansion is a key growth driver.

companies.name: On Holding AG
companies.business_model: Premium performance running and lifestyle footwear and apparel brand. Sells DTC via e-commerce and branded stores alongside selective wholesale (Foot Locker, Nordstrom, etc.). Known for proprietary CloudTec sole technology. Has entered apparel and accessories. Strong innovation and design positioning.
companies.target_audience: Performance and lifestyle consumers aged 20–45. Sold in 60+ countries.
companies.notes: One of the fastest-growing premium footwear brands globally. Roger Federer is a co-owner and ambassador. Strong DTC growth and international expansion trajectory. High valuations relative to peers.

companies.name: Ralph Lauren Corporation
companies.business_model: Global premium lifestyle brand selling apparel, accessories, home, and fragrance through its own retail stores, e-commerce, and wholesale (department stores). Known for aspirational American luxury aesthetic. Multiple price-tier brands under portfolio. Strong brand equity and global recognition.
companies.target_audience: Premium consumers aged 25–65. Present in 55+ countries across all price tiers.
companies.notes: One of the most enduring premium American lifestyle brands. Has done well repositioning upmarket. DTC growth and international expansion have been key strategic priorities. Club Monaco sold in 2020.

companies.name: Columbia Sportswear Company
companies.business_model: Multi-brand outdoor and active lifestyle apparel, footwear, and equipment company. Sells through wholesale (department stores, outdoor retailers), DTC stores, and e-commerce. Designs and markets products globally with manufacturing outsourced. Family-controlled company (Boyle family).
companies.target_audience: Outdoor and active consumers aged 25–55. Sold in 90+ countries.
companies.notes: Strong wholesale business and global distribution. Less fashion-forward than peers but solid fundamentals. prAna is sustainability-focused. Sorel has stronger lifestyle/fashion crossover appeal.

companies.name: Birkenstock Holding
companies.business_model: Premium lifestyle footwear brand built around anatomical cork-latex footbed technology. Sells through selective wholesale (Nordstrom, specialty retailers), DTC stores, and e-commerce. Brand has repositioned from orthopaedic/functional into fashion-lifestyle crossover with premium pricing. Very selective distribution to protect brand equity.
companies.target_audience: Comfort and lifestyle consumers aged 20–65. Expanded into fashion demographics post-2023. Sold in 100+ countries.
companies.notes: Recently IPO'd (2023). One of the most culturally interesting cases. Barbie movie association in 2023 was a significant brand moment. Selective distribution is a deliberate brand protection strategy. L Catterton (LVMH-affiliated) is a major shareholder.
